# `silk/crypto/blake2s`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Portable BLAKE2s-256 state for the unkeyed 32-byte cryptographic digest of RFC 7693.

## When to use
Use [`Blake2s256`](#Blake2s256) where a format names BLAKE2s with a 32-byte digest, such as Node's
`blake2s256` hash. Use `silk.crypto.blake2b` for BLAKE2b and `silk.crypto.sha2` where a
protocol names SHA-2.

## Details
The state supports incremental input through `update`, consuming finalization through `finish`,
and one-shot input through `hash`. It uses only inline storage and allocates no memory. The
digest is the little-endian encoding of the final state words, as RFC 7693 specifies.

## Gotchas
Keyed hashing, salts, personalization and digest lengths other than 32 bytes are not supported.
If an update makes the message longer than 2^64 - 1 bytes, the program traps.

## Examples
### Hash a short message
```silk
import silk.crypto.blake2s {Blake2s256}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let digest = Blake2s256.hash(b"abc")
  // BLAKE2s-256("abc") is 508c5e8c...5982.
  if digest[0] != 0x50 || digest[31] != 0x82 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Blake2s256` with `import silk.crypto.blake2s { Blake2s256 }`.

Public declarations: 1.

## `Blake2s256`

```silk
pub struct Blake2s256
```

An incremental unkeyed BLAKE2s state with a 32-byte digest (RFC 7693).

### Details

Give input in parts with [`Blake2s256.update`](#Blake2s256.impl.update) and get the digest with [`Blake2s256.finish`](#Blake2s256.impl.finish),
or hash one slice with [`Blake2s256.hash`](#Blake2s256.impl.hash). The state uses only inline storage and allocates no
memory.

### Gotchas

Keyed hashing, salts, personalization and digest lengths other than 32 bytes are not supported.
If an update makes the message longer than 2^64 - 1 bytes, the program traps.

<a id="Blake2s256.impl.update"></a>

### Method `update`

```silk
pub fn update(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8]) -> ()
```

Adds `bytes` to this state in source order. An empty slice does not change the state.

#### Details
A full block is compressed only when more input follows it, because the final block is
compressed with the finalization flag. It allocates no memory.
